rv.q: I think Huang does want to debate the pill's complexity but she can't help but stack the deck.
The Birth of the Pill is that one Must-See play of the year that everyone should see.
Timeline Theatre's world premiere of The Birth of the Pill is part history lesson, part inventive comedy, part provocative drama, and fully not to be missed.
This play is deadly serious and highly entertaining.
This will be a big hit for TimeLine and a tough ticket in the weeks ahead.
THE BIRTH OF THE PILL is a fascinating portrayal of what it takes to move a controversial idea into a universal solution.
The Birth of the Pill has the intellectual honesty to acknowledge the unethical aspects of the human trials of the pill.
As always at TimeLine Theatre, History comes alive in Sandra Marquez’s excellent production.
The timeliness of Huang’s play is unquestionable.
The 90-minute production feels like a book, more telling than showing, although the comprehensive proscenium set...provides an appropriate background shorthand for experimentation.
This is an amazing year for Timeline Theatre!
After an extension announcement, it is clear this is a play from TimeLine Theatre one should not miss this fall season.

cn.t: Timeline's world premiere earns mostly positive reviews for its informative, entertaining approach to contraceptive history, though some critics fault its adaptation choices and handling of the Puerto Rican trial subjects.
